title: Credibility Assessment of Implicit Finite Element Models for Spinal Pedicle Screw Pullout and Bone Purchase
device: Thoracolumbar pedicle screw and vertebral fixation construct

models.name: Model A: Thread-Resolved Screw–Bone Contact Model
models.what_it_computes: Implicit quasi-static FEA of a pedicle screw engaging a vertebral segment with resolved thread geometry, nonlinear frictional contact to cortical shell and cancellous core, capturing axial pullout response, local bone stress/strain fields, interfacial slip, and purchase stiffness.

models.name: Model B: Density-Mapped Damage–Plasticity Bone Model with Cohesive Interface
models.what_it_computes: Implicit quasi-static FEA using CT-derived density-to-modulus mapping for cancellous bone, orthotropic cortical shell, pressure-overclosure contact, cohesive elements at the thread–bone interface, computing insertion-torque surrogate, micromotion under bending, cyclic degradation, and shear cut-out resistance.

mechanisms.name: Monotonic axial pullout
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Defines peak holding capacity and post-yield energy absorption that govern acute loss of fixation during aggressive reduction maneuvers.

mechanisms.name: Cyclic craniocaudal toggling
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Represents repetitive rocking from physiologic loading that can degrade thread engagement and lead to progressive loosening.

mechanisms.name: Insertion torque–purchase relationship
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Links intraoperative torque or surrogate quantities to initial bone purchase, informing immediate stability without destructive testing.

mechanisms.name: Medial–lateral shear cut-out
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Assesses resistance to transverse loads that can cause thread plowing and pedicle wall compromise, especially in weak bone.

ambiguous_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–7 Credibility Readiness Scale (CRS), with anchors at 0 (no evidence), 3 (foundational), 5 (decision-ready), and 7 (mission-ready), for each model-by-mechanism pair.
